title: Associate Director, Clinical Supply Management (UK/EU)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p></p> <p><strong>About Summit:</strong></p> <p>Summit Therapeutics Inc. is a biopharmaceutical oncology company with a mission focused on improving quality of life, increasing potential duration of life, and resolving serious unmet medical needs. At Summit, we believe in building a team of world class professionals who are passionate about this mission, and it is our people who drive this mission to reality. Summit’s core values include integrity, passion for excellence, purposeful urgency, collaboration, and our commitment to people. Our employees are truly the heart and soul of our culture, and they are invaluable in shaping our journey toward excellence.</p> <p>Summit’s team is inspired to touch and help change lives through Summit’s clinical studies in the field of oncology. Summit has multiple global Phase 3 clinical studies, including:</p> <p><strong>Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>HARMONi: Phase 3 clinical study which was intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who were previously treated with a 3rd generation EGFR TKI.</p> </li> </ul> <ul> <li> <p>HARMONi-3: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.</p> </li> </ul> <ul> <li> <p>HARMONi-7: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab monotherapy compared to pembrolizumab monotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Colorectal Cancer (CRC)</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>HARMONi-GI3: Phase 3 clinical study intended to evaluate ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy compared with bevacizumab plus chemotherapy.</p> </li> </ul> <p><em>Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy not presently approved by any regulatory authority other than China’s National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). Summit is headquartered in Miami, Florida, and has additional offices in California, New Jersey, the UK, and Ireland.</em></p> <p></p></div><p><strong><span style="font-size: 10.5pt;">Job Title: Sr. Medical Science Liaison</span></strong></p> <p><strong><span style="font-size: 10.5pt;">Location: Oxford, UK or Zug, Switzerland or Dublin, Ireland</span></strong></p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Overview of Role:</strong></p> <p>The Associate Director, Clinical Supply Management supports the Senior Director in leading the full scope of global clinical supply chain responsibilities. The role translates functional strategy into disciplined execution across demand and supply planning, inventory management, packaging and labelling, distribution, returns and destruction, cross-border compliance, and GxP operations. Acting as a key delegate for the Senior Director, the (Associate) Director provides a layer of management for direct reports, establishes clear priorities and performance expectations, develops team capability, and drives operational excellence through standardized processes, meaningful metrics, proactive risk management, and continuous improvement. The role partners closely with Clinical Operations, Commercial, CMC, Quality, Regulatory, Finance, Legal, Procurement, Medical Affairs and Program Management, and oversees external partners including Contract Development and Manufacturing Organizations (CDMOs), IXRS providers and specialist service providers.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Role and Responsibilities:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Supports the Senior Director in developing functional strategy, operating plans, budgets, governance and performance objectives across global clinical supply chain activities</li> <li>Leads day-to-day execution for new and ongoing studies and products, ensuring robust forecasting, supply planning, schedule adherence, inventory optimization, global logistics and sustained GxP compliance</li> <li>Serves as a delegate for the Senior Director in cross-functional forums, governance meetings, supplier reviews and issue escalation, providing clear recommendations and ensuring timely follow-through.</li> <li>Manages and develops direct reports, translating functional priorities into individual objectives, balancing workloads, coaching performance, supporting career development and ensuring appropriate succession and capability plans.</li> <li>Creates an effective management layer by coordinating team activities, reinforcing accountability, removing operational barriers and escalating material risks or decisions to the Senior Director.</li> <li>Overseeing the Clinical Supply Management (CSM) team, the Associate Director interprets complex clinical protocols, development plans and commercial demand forecasts, working with CMC and internal and external partners to develop packaging, labelling, supply and resupply strategies, timelines and plans.</li> <li>Supports the accountability of CSM team to oversee packaging, labelling, release, distribution, resupply, returns, reconciliation and destruction activities across global locations</li> <li>Develops and maintains supply project budgets, resource plans and integrated schedules, monitors performance and proactively resolves variances</li> <li>Manages CDMO and service-provider activities from RFP and contracting support through routine operations, troubleshooting, invoicing and performance management using defined KPIs and service expectations</li> <li>Supports IXRS selection, design, set-up, User Acceptance Testing (UAT), implementation and ongoing operational performance as required by IRT Management Team.</li> <li>Drives operational excellence by defining standard work, governance routines, KPIs and dashboards; uses trend and root-cause analysis to improve service, quality, cost, compliance and team productivity</li> <li>Leads continuous-improvement initiatives that streamline and harmonize processes, strengthen inspection readiness and embed sustainable ways of working</li> <li>Supports regulatory submissions, audits and inspections and ensures timely management of SOPs, change controls, deviations, investigations and CAPAs within the function</li> <li>Provides continuity of leadership and performs other responsibilities within the function as assigned</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Experience, Education and Specialized Knowledge and Skills:</strong></p> <ul> <li>BSc, MSc, engineering or pharmacy degree, or equivalent, with a minimum of 8+ years of progressive supply chain experience in a pharmaceutical, biotechnology or contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) environment</li> <li>Demonstrated success leading complex international clinical studies and product supply chains, with broad knowledge of regulatory and GMP requirements for IMP and commercial product packaging and supply</li> <li>Prior people-management experience, including setting objectives, coaching performance, developing talent, delegating effectively and managing through others</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into executable priorities, operating rhythms, metrics and measurable team outcomes</li> <li>Strong operational-excellence and continuous-improvement capability, including process standardization, KPI management, root-cause analysis and sustainable implementation of improvements</li> <li>Solid understanding of IXRS design specifications, set-up and UAT, together with proficiency in clinical supply planning and forecasting tools</li> <li>Strong project, budget, risk and resource-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining high-quality results</li> <li>Expertise in outsourcing, supplier governance, negotiation and performance management</li> <li>Experience building, scaling or improving end-to-end product supply chains and associated business processes</li> <li>Ability to operate as a trusted deputy to the Director, exercise sound judgement within delegated authority and escalate issues with clear options and recommendations</li> <li>Confident communicator able to influence all levels of the organization and build effective relationships with global colleagues, customers and suppliers</li> <li>Able to work independently with complex global problems while fostering inclusion, collaboration, accountability and effective team leadership</li> <li>Agile and resilient in a dynamic organization where priorities may change raw.description:
About EH Group Engineering

EHG is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product is a significantly more compact fuel cell with high power density and lower costs of production. Faced with the challenges of climate change and the transition to a decentralised energy system, EHG seeks to provide high performance and cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

To help bring this vision to life, we are looking for a Senior Control Engineer to coordinate our efforts in designing control strategies for containerized systems integrating our fuel cell technology alongside equipment such as gas reformers, batteries, and climate control units. You will coordinate the control team and play a key role in shaping how these complex, multi-equipment systems operate safely and efficiently in the field.

Based in the US? You’re welcome to apply. This is an on-site role in Nyon, Switzerland. We ask that you relocate within 3 months of starting, and we’ll support you with a relocation package.

 

Key Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate the control engineering activities and define the control architecture and technical roadmap for our fuel cell and containerized power systems

  • Develop control strategies, models and algorithms for test-benches, fuel cell system and containerized power supply systems using Matlab/Simulink and Siemens PLCs

  • Coordinate the transition of prototype control algorithms from Simulink to industrial-quality code in TIA Portal Step 7

  • Implement, tune and validate controllers for thermal, air, fuel and power subsystems

  • Define and own control requirements, state machines and safety/diagnostic logic

  • Drive the continuous improvement (performance, efficiency and robustness) of our products

  • Define and oversee model-in-the-loop (MIL) testing and validation procedures

  • Manage the complete software life cycle, from requirements through release and maintenance, including dataset management

  • Establish coding standards, conduct code reviews and ensure compliance with industrial and certification requirements

  • Coordinate and develop the control team, including task planning and prioritization

  • Act as the main control interface with embedded, test and electrical engineering, as well as external partners and suppliers

 

Skills and Experience Required:

  • BSc/MSc in control, electrical, mechatronic or automation engineering is mandatory

  • Minimum 7 years of experience in control engineering, including at least 2 years in a technical lead or senior role

  • Skill 1 : Strong experience in process control engineering, particularly with containerized power supply systems; knowledge of programming and implementing safety PLCs is a strong plus

  • Skill 2 : Strong experience with TIA Portal (Step 7, WinCC, Test Suite), with the ability to structure code to industrial standards and meet certification requirements

  • Experience with functional safety (e.g. IEC 61508, ISO 13849), including SIL/PL determination and implementation of safety functions

  • Experience across the complete V-model development cycle, including hazard and risk assessment, requirements definition, safety requirements specification (SRS), verification and validation, and dataset management

  • Experience with stationary and maritime power applications, with a focus on the US and EU markets and their respective standards and certification requirements

  • Proven team player, with the ability to:
    (i) Coordinate and mentor the control team by clearly explaining your code and helping the team adopt robust industrial methods: you will take the responsibility in developing Skill 1 and Skill 2 across the team
    (ii) Collaborate effectively within interdisciplinary teams

  • Solid knowledge of control theory, state machines and system identification

  • Strong experience with MATLAB/Simulink and model-based design is a plus

  • Professional working language is in English.

     

Start date: Immediately

To help bring this vision to life, we are looking for a Senior Control Engineer to coordinate our efforts in designing control strategies for containerized systems integrating our fuel cell technology alongside equipment such as gas reformers, batteries, and climate control units. You will coordinate the control team and play a key role in shaping how these complex, multi-equipment systems operate safely and efficiently in the field.

Based in the US? You’re welcome to apply. This is an on-site role in Nyon, Switzerland. We ask that you relocate within 3 months of starting, and we’ll support you with a relocation package.

 

Key Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate the control engineering activities and define the control architecture and technical roadmap for our fuel cell and containerized power systems

  • Develop control strategies, models and algorithms for test-benches, fuel cell system and containerized power supply systems using Matlab/Simulink and Siemens PLCs

  • Coordinate the transition of prototype control algorithms from Simulink to industrial-quality code in TIA Portal Step 7

  • Implement, tune and validate controllers for thermal, air, fuel and power subsystems

  • Define and own control requirements, state machines and safety/diagnostic logic

  • Drive the continuous improvement (performance, efficiency and robustness) of our products

  • Define and oversee model-in-the-loop (MIL) testing and validation procedures

  • Manage the complete software life cycle, from requirements through release and maintenance, including dataset management

  • Establish coding standards, conduct code reviews and ensure compliance with industrial and certification requirements

  • Coordinate and develop the control team, including task planning and prioritization

  • Act as the main control interface with embedded, test and electrical engineering, as well as external partners and suppliers

 

Skills and Experience Required:

  • BSc/MSc in control, electrical, mechatronic or automation engineering is mandatory

  • Minimum 7 years of experience in control engineering, including at least 2 years in a technical lead or senior role

  • Skill 1 : Strong experience in process control engineering, particularly with containerized power supply systems; knowledge of programming and implementing safety PLCs is a strong plus

  • Skill 2 : Strong experience with TIA Portal (Step 7, WinCC, Test Suite), with the ability to structure code to industrial standards and meet certification requirements

  • Experience across the complete V-model development cycle, including hazard and risk assessment, requirements definition, safety requirements specification (SRS), verification and validation, and dataset management

  • Experience with stationary and maritime power applications, with a focus on the US and EU markets and their respective standards and certification requirements

  • Proven team player, with the ability to:
    (i) Coordinate and mentor the control team by clearly explaining your code and helping the team adopt robust industrial methods: you will take the responsibility in developing Skill 1 and Skill 2 across the team
    (ii) Collaborate effectively within interdisciplinary teams

  • Solid knowledge of control theory, state machines and system identification

  • Strong experience with MATLAB/Simulink and model-based design is a plus

  • Professional working language is in English.

     

Start date: Immediately

Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US.

 

What you'll own

  • One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland.

  • Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one.

  • In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.

  • Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.

  • Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria.

  • Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other.

  • Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities.

  • Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant.

  • Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly.

  • Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow.

 

What we're looking for

Core experience

  • Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance.

  • Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one.

  • Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability.

  • Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard.

  • Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects.

  • Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage.

  • The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure.

  • Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely.

Especially compelling

  • Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience.

  • Experience with cleanliness-critical or contamination-sensitive assembly processes.

  • Experience supporting a technology transfer between sites or countries, and establishing quality at the receiving end.

  • Experience qualifying and auditing contract manufacturers or system integrators.

  • Startup or scale-up experience as an early hire during hyper-growth.

  • Experience working between Europe and the US, and with US codes and certification practice in particular. French is useful but not required.

 

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, calibrated to the market and discussed directly with you.

  • Relocation support to Nyon, Switzerland.

  • The opportunity to build EHG's global quality function during a defining phase of hyper-growth.

Note: Swiss work authorization or eligibility is required for this role, along with the ability to travel to the United States.

 

EH Group is an equal opportunity employer. Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company.

 

The opportunity

We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas.

You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that.

Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets.

Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US.

 

What you'll own

  • One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland.

  • Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one.

  • In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.

  • Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.

  • Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria.

  • Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other.

  • Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities.

  • Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant.

  • Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly.

  • Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow.

 

What we're looking for

Core experience

  • Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance.

  • Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one.

  • Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability.

  • Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard.

  • Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects.

  • Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage.

  • The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure.

  • Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely.

Especially compelling

  • Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience.

  • Experience with cleanliness-critical or contamination-sensitive assembly processes.

  • Experience supporting a technology transfer between sites or countries, and establishing quality at the receiving end.

  • Experience qualifying and auditing contract manufacturers or system integrators.

  • Startup or scale-up experience as an early hire during hyper-growth.

  • Experience working between Europe and the US, and with US codes and certification practice in particular. French is useful but not required.

 

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, calibrated to the market and discussed directly with you.

  • Relocation support to Nyon, Switzerland.

  • The opportunity to build EHG's global quality function during a defining phase of hyper-growth.

raw.title: Global Quality Manager - Fuel Cell Manufacturing
raw.description:
About EHG

EH Group (EHG) is a rapidly growing fuel cell power platform delivering onsite power to AI data centers, defense, and industry. Our fuel-agnostic proton exchange membrane (PEM) systems scale from kW-scale units to GW-scale power plants, and we design, manufacture, and deploy them for customers worldwide.

Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company.

 

The opportunity

We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas.

You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that.

Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets.

Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US.

 

What you'll own

  • One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland.

  • Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one.

  • In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.

  • Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.

  • Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria.

  • Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other.

  • Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities.

  • Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant.

  • Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly.

  • Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow.

 

What we're looking for

Core experience

  • Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance.

  • Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one.

  • Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability.

  • Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard.

  • Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects.

  • Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage.

  • The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure.

  • Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely.

Especially compelling

  • Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience.

This is a senior scientist who owns assay quality, data QC and controls, and production troubleshooting across the entire experimental pipeline. The production team runs 150+ experiments per month across expression, BLI, SPR, thermostability, and enzyme activity. When something goes wrong (failed expression, anomalous binding data, instrument artifacts), this person diagnoses the root cause and fixes it. As the assay and instrumentation portfolio expands, this person translates new R&D methods into production-ready protocols, builds robust methods that junior technicians can execute reliably, and designs comprehensive controls that enable automated QC and data processing. This is a player-coach position. You will still run experiments personally, especially as you integrate into the lab, but you will also elevate the whole team's capabilities. What You'll Do Troubleshoot production failures across the full pipeline. A batch of proteins isn't expressing: is it the construct design, the expression system, or the media? BLI sensorgrams look noisy: is it the sensor tips, the sample prep, or an instrument issue? You figure it out, fix it, and make the cause easier to identify next time. Develop and document SOPs for new assays as the portfolio expands. Take methods from the R&D team and make them production-ready: robust, reproducible, and executable by junior technicians without hand-holding. Mentor a growing production team. Set quality standards, review data, train new hires, and build a culture where people flag problems early instead of hiding them. Work at the intersection of biology, automation, and QC. Collaborate with researchers, laboratory technicians, and automation engineers on protocol optimization for work cells, and with software on LabOS protocol integration. Own the relationship between assay science and throughput. The easy version of every assay doesn't scale, and the scalable version often sacrifices quality. You find the right tradeoff. What We're Looking For Deep hands-on expertise in protein production: expression (E. coli, mammalian, cell-free), purification (IMAC, SEC), and biophysical characterization (BLI and SPR at minimum). This isn't negotiable. You need to have done this work yourself, at volume. PhD in protein biochemistry, biophysics, or structural biology, plus 3-5 years in a production or development role at a CRO, foundry, or high-throughput lab. Academic postdocs count if the work was high-throughput and production-oriented. Experience with high-throughput workflows. You're comfortable with 96-well plates and liquid handlers, not just single-column purifications. You've optimized protocols for scale, not just for one perfect result. Mentorship mindset. You've managed or trained junior scientists before. You enjoy teaching and get satisfaction from watching your team grow. Troubleshooting instinct. When data looks wrong, your first impulse is to understand why, not to rerun the experiment and hope it works. Quality-obsessed but pragmatic. You care deeply about data quality, but you also understand that production has deadlines and sometimes "good enough" is the right call. Bridge between R&D and production. You can speak both languages: the exploratory mindset of research and the reproducibility demands of production. raw.title: IoT Embedded Systems Engineer
raw.description:
• Take ownership of the development of IoT systems, with a focus on embedded software, system architecture, and hardware and firmware integration

  • Design and develop robust, efficient, and scalable embedded software for IoT products based on microcontroller platforms and, optionally, Linux based systems

  • Provide technical guidance for hardware development in collaboration with external partners, including reviewing and challenging PCB designs to ensure functionality, quality, and manufacturability

  • Collaborate closely with mechanical, software, and cloud engineering teams to ensure seamless end to end system integration

  • Define and refine product requirements from initial concept through to mass production in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders

  • Develop and integrate prototypes and support the transition from development into serial production together with manufacturing partners

  • Contribute to the continuous evolution of the embedded platform, including MCU based solutions as well as optional Linux and Yocto based components

  • Develop pragmatic testing strategies to ensure the functionality, reliability, and quality of both hardware and firmware

  • Support development and manufacturing partners with debugging, technical documentation, and production ramp up

  • Provide Level 3 technical support for complex system, firmware, and hardware related issues

  • Travel approximately 5 to 10 percent to support development partners, product validation activities, and product launches


  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Embedded Systems, Computer Science, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience

  • Several years of hands on experience in embedded development, including firmware development and hardware related engineering

  • Strong understanding of hardware design and PCB layouts, with the ability to review design decisions and collaborate effectively with hardware development teams

  • Strong expertise in embedded firmware development and software architecture for microcontroller platforms such as ARM Cortex, ESP32, or STM32

  • Experience with sensor integration and wireless communication technologies such as BLE and WiFi

  • Experience with embedded Linux systems, particularly Yocto, is an advantage, especially in environments combining System on Modules with MCU based architectures

  • Broad system level understanding of mechanics, sensors, actuators, and their integration into robust IoT products

  • Hands on experience with hardware testing, debugging tools, and automated production testing

  • Familiarity with certification standards such as CE and FCC is an advantage

  • Fluent in German and English, with additional languages considered a plus

title: Manager Operations Planning & Performance
description: Bij Crisp hebben we een missie: eten met meer smaak bereikbaar maken voor iedereen. Daarvoor moet elke schakel in onze operatie, van warehouse tot voordeur, dagelijks naadloos op elkaar aansluiten. Als Manager Operations Planning & Performance ben jij de spil tussen wat de klant bestelt en hoe wij dat logistiek waarmaken. Je brengt alle operationele schakels samen in één strakke, integrale planning en bouwt mee aan een betrouwbare operatie die klaar is om slim door te groeien. Wat je gaat doen Je bent eigenaar van de integrale operationele planning. Je vertaalt verwachte klantvraag naar concrete capaciteit op de weg (hoeveel bezorgers hebben we per dag en per hub nodig?) en bepaalt samen met de Operations Manager de planningsstrategie voor de korte en middellange termijn. Je zorgt voor een strakke planning tussen Delivery, Retentie en Warehouse. Zo werkt iedereen vanuit dezelfde basis en tilt jouw scherpe blik onze processen naar een hoger niveau. Je geeft leiding aan een team van routeplanners (werkstudenten en starters). Samen zorgen jullie dagelijks voor de meest efficiënte bezorgroutes. Jouw team staat in direct contact met de bezorghubs, het warehouse en de growth afdeling om de capaciteit af te stemmen Je werkt nauw samen met teams door de hele organisatie, van Tech en Analytics tot Recruitment. Om te weten wat er speelt, ben je regelmatig te vinden waar het gebeurt: op onze bezorghubs en in het warehouse. Je stuurt op operationele KPI’s (zoals Drops per Hour en Time per Stop ) en beheert belangrijke kostenlijnen. Samen met de Regiomanager en Business Analyst Delivery blijf je ons bezorgnetwerk continu optimaliseren. Je bent eindverantwoordelijk voor de lijn tussen ons warehouse en de hubs. Je onderhoudt de contacten met vrachtwagenvervoerders, stuurt op prestaties ( On Time ) en kosten ( Cost per Drop ) en maximaliseert de vulgraad. Je kijkt altijd naar wat beter kan, houdt trends en innovaties in de markt in de gaten en draagt dit actief aan wanneer je hier kansen ziet. Je signaleert kansen in de operatie, maakt de impact inzichtelijk en leidt verbeterprojecten van idee tot implementatie, bijvoorbeeld op het gebied van servicetijd, automatisering van planningstaken of de inrichting van ons netwerk. Je bent onderdeel van het Delivery team en rapporteert aan de Head of Delivery. Dit ben jij Je hebt HBO/WO werk- en denkniveau en minimaal 3 jaar werkervaring in operationele planning, logistiek of supply chain, bij voorkeur in een snelgroeiende e-commerce- of retailomgeving. Je beweegt je makkelijk door de hele organisatie, van de vloer tot het management. Je zoekt actief de samenwerking op en krijgt verschillende teams moeiteloos op één lijn. Je creëert draagvlak en krijgt mensen mee in een gezamenlijke aanpak, ook als je geen formele zeggenschap over ze hebt Je bent sterk met data. Je duikt zelf in de cijfers, bouwt een model of dashboard als dat nodig is, en vertaalt analyses naar concrete keuzes voor de operatie. Ervaring met SQL, BigQuery en Data Studio is een pré. Jij kijkt verder dan je eigen scope en overziet de hele keten. Je begrijpt hoe een keuze in de planning doorwerkt in het warehouse, op de weg en bij de klant, en je weet de juiste balans te vinden tussen kosten en kwaliteit. Je bent resultaatgericht en weet wat het is om eigenaarschap te nemen. Jij maakt dingen graag makkelijk en concreet. Complexe vraagstukken zet jij gemakkelijk om naar begrijpelijke acties. Je houdt het hoofd koel als het even spannend wordt. Pieken, onverwachte uitval of last-minute wijzigingen brengen je niet van je stuk; je prioriteert, plant opnieuw en zorgt dat de operatie doordraait. Je spreekt vloeiend Nederlands en Engels. Wat wij bieden Werken bij een B Corp gecertificeerd bedrijf, waarbij je de kans krijgt om je stempel te drukken op het Europese voedselsysteem. 27 vakantiedagen om bij te komen en op te laden. Een extra vrije dag per jaar om je in te zetten voor vrijwilligerswerk en iets goeds te doen. Aandacht voor je mentale gezondheid met online begeleiding van erkende psychologen via OpenUp. Voor straks een perfect pensioen via BPFL. Elke maand food for thought, met workshops en talks via de Crisp University. Regelmatig tastings of workshops op kantoor of bij een van onze leveranciers, om te zien hoe onze lekkerste producten worden gemaakt – en natuurlijk ook te proeven. Dagelijks een uitgebreide, georganiseerde lunch op kantoor. Enthousiaste, slimme collega’s en tijd om elkaar te leren kennen tijdens sport, events en proeverijen. En... fikse korting op je Crisp boodschappen, omdat je thuis natuurlijk ook goed wilt eten. Onze selectieprocedure Solliciteer via onderstaande button. Hoe meer je kunt delen over jezelf en de reden dat je solliciteert, hoe beter. Bij Crisp streven we naar een inclusieve en diverse werkomgeving waarin iedereen welkom is, ongeacht hun achtergrond, geslacht, leeftijd, etniciteit, seksuele geaardheid, religie of beperking. Wij moedigen sollicitanten met diverse perspectieven en achtergronden aan om te solliciteren en geloven in gelijke kansen voor iedereen. We waarderen de unieke bijdragen die elke medewerker kan leveren en zijn vastbesloten om een inclusieve werkplek te creëren waarin iedereen wordt gerespecteerd en gewaardeerd. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

title: Project Leider Bouw
description: Monumental automatiseert de bouw met robotica en software. Onze missie is om de bouw software-defined en autonoom te maken – een toekomst waarin mooie gebouwen op maat in één dag verrijzen, met minimale inzet van handwerk. We zijn een groeiend team van engineers, operators en technici, afkomstig van bedrijven als Palantir, Qualcomm, Dyson, Shopify, Tesla, Meta en Google DeepMind. We staan nog aan het begin van het opbouwen van dit bedrijf, en dit is je kans om buitenproportioneel veel impact te maken op een probleem dat écht uitmaakt. Vanaf dag één werk je samen met een ervaren foundingteam, met een Series B van $32M achter ons onder leiding van Khosla Ventures en Plural. Monumental zit in het centrum van Amsterdam, in een prachtig pand met een volledig uitgeruste werkplaats en een eigen testvloer voor robots. We bouwen de hele stack in-house – hardware én software. We zijn uitdrukkelijk geen hybride of remote-first bedrijf: robots en muren bouw je niet vanaf je keukentafel, dus we werken vijf dagen per week op locatie. Lees meer over waarom wij vinden dat je je tijd aan de bouw zou moeten besteden, en over onze visie en ons bedrijf . Misschien vind je ons YouTube-kanaal interessant, de film van Based in Europe over hoe we het Europese woningtekort aanpakken , of deze video van Andreas Klinger over hoe ons kantoor eruitziet. Over de functie De afgelopen jaren is Monumental gegroeid van een werkend product en de eerste proefprojecten naar bouwen op grote schaal. Inmiddels hebben we een vloot van meer dan 150 robots, die metselwerk hebben uitgevoerd voor meer dan 90 woningen, een school, een buurthuis, een hotel en meer dan 150 meter kanaalwand. Elke maand nemen we meer bouwprojecten aan, intern noemen we die ‘deployments’. We werken met meer robots en meer mensen en breiden vanuit Nederland uit naar het Verenigd Koninkrijk en de VS. Als Hub Lead zet je onze eerste vestiging buiten het hoofdkantoor op, in het noorden van Nederland. Je begint met ons grootste bouwproject tot nu toe. Naarmate er meer projecten bijkomen, bouw je het team en de operatie verder uit. We zoeken mensen die breed inzetbaar zijn en een bouwproject willen leiden alsof het hun eigen bedrijf is. Achter elk project staat een Deployment Manager die van begin tot eind verantwoordelijk is. In de praktijk vervul je vijf rollen tegelijk: uitvoerder, operationeel manager, accountmanager, analist en projectmanager. Je maakt het bouwplan, voert het met je team als onderaannemer uit, onderhoudt het contact met de aannemer en zorgt dat we goed metselwerk op tijd opleveren. Dat doe je in de bouw, waar plannen voortdurend veranderen. Uiteindelijk leid je meerdere projecten tegelijk, waaronder complexe projecten waarbij veel op het spel staat. De ene dag sta je bij zonsopgang op en ga je naar de bouwplaats. Je zaagt stenen, bewaakt de planning, stemt af met de hoofdaannemer en ziet je bouwplan steen voor steen werkelijkheid worden. De volgende dag zit je op onze vestiging, analyseer je de winst- en verliesrekening van je project en werk je aan systemen waarmee je bij het volgende project een betere marge haalt. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de oplevering en geeft knelpunten die je op de bouwplaats tegenkomt door aan ons R&D-team. Dit is intensief, praktisch werk op locatie, waar je veel voldoening uit kunt halen. Robots gaan kapot, het weer slaat om en de aannemer verandert het plan. Jij zorgt dat de bouw doorgaat. Je krijgt veel vrijheid en verantwoordelijkheid. De rol past goed bij je als je eerder een bedrijf hebt opgericht, of als je een ondernemende functie zoekt waarin je veel invloed hebt op het resultaat. Wat je gaat doen De logistiek van een bouwproject plannen. Je bepaalt hoeveel en welke robots en mensen nodig zijn, stemt af met andere onderaannemers en maakt de dagelijkse planning. Tegelijk houd je het grotere geheel in het oog en begrijp je wat jouw keuzes betekenen voor de kosten en opbrengsten per project. Op de bouwplaats het team aansturen, begeleiden en motiveren. Je onderhoudt het contact met hoofdaannemers en andere betrokkenen, vertegenwoordigt Monumental en legt uit wat we doen. Je schakelt net zo makkelijk met steigerbouwers als met de CEO’s van de grootste hoofdaannemers en onze engineers. Operationele systemen opzetten waarmee elk project beter verloopt dan het vorige. Je ziet waar tijd en middelen verloren gaan, past processen aan en verbetert de marge. Samenwerken met bestaande klanten en zorgen dat daar nieuwe bouwprojecten uit voortkomen. In de toekomst doe je dat ook voor aanverwante productlijnen buiten het metselwerk. Verantwoordelijkheid nemen voor de winst- en verliesrekening van je project en voorstellen doen om de kosten en opbrengsten per project steeds verder te verbeteren. Helpen bij het werven en interviewen van nieuwe robotoperators en deployment operators. Wat we zoeken Minimaal drie jaar ervaring startupervaring, als operator, manager, of founder. Nederlands als moedertaal. De bouwsector is sterk lokaal georganiseerd, dus dit is een vereiste voor de functie. Je communiceert helder en makkelijk met mensen met uiteenlopende achtergronden. Je bent bereid om letterlijk je handen vuil te maken om het werk gedaan te krijgen. Je komt snel in actie, zet door en krijgt dingen voor elkaar. In deze functie draait het vooral om uitvoeren. Je kunt goed omgaan met hoge werkdruk. Op bouwplaatsen gaat regelmatig iets mis en staat er veel op het spel. Daar komt bij dat we nieuwe technologie inzetten waarvan we nog niet alle mogelijke storingen kennen. Je denkt scherp en leert graag. Welke achtergrond je ook hebt, je zult in deze rol veel en snel moeten leren. Het werk kan elke drie tot zes maanden als een nieuwe baan voelen. Je leert veel over de bouw, robotica en werken in een snelgroeiend technologiebedrijf. Je hebt ervaring met het aansturen van een klein team en weet hoe je mensen begeleidt en motiveert. Je bent operationeel en analytisch sterk. Je kunt een helder operationeel plan uitwerken in een spreadsheet, een winst- en verliesrekening presenteren en verschillende scenario’s doorrekenen, inclusief de factoren die het resultaat bepalen. Je bent een sterke projectmanager. Waarom Monumental? Bij Monumental werken betekent vooroplopen in een beweging die de bouwsector wezenlijk wil veranderen. Jouw werk heeft hier niet alleen impact op het bedrijf, maar op de toekomst van hoe we bouwen. Als je gedreven wordt door innovatie, graag complexe uitdagingen aanpakt en klaar bent om echt verschil te maken, horen we graag van je. Voor open sollicitaties (als je geen rol ziet die precies past) kun je ons mailen op: Helaas bieden we op dit moment geen stageplekken aan. Voldoe je niet aan alle eisen hierboven, maar ben je enthousiast over Monumental en denk je dat je ons toch kunt helpen moeilijke problemen op te lossen? Neem dan contact op. We verwelkomen generalisten die op resultaat gericht zijn en graag on the job leren. Find Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

raw.title: Team Lead, Data Engineering
raw.description:
We are looking for a Data Engineering Team Lead to lead the Data Platform team at DataSnipper.

Every decision DataSnipper makes about its products runs through the data platform: which features land, which customers are getting value, what we bill for, what we fix next, and which AI capabilities add the most value. You will lead a team of two data engineers who own the systems that make that possible. That means how usage events get captured across a growing set of products, how they become trustworthy models in Snowflake, and how Customer Success, Product and GTM get to answers without waiting on us.

This is a player-coach role in a small, high-ownership team. You are responsible for the people, the roadmap and the technical direction, and you stay hands-on enough to ship alongside the team and make architectural calls credibly. At DataSnipper, Team Lead is our entry point into engineering management: the same people, delivery and product responsibilities as an Engineering Manager, on a smaller team.

We are a handful of people serving the whole company, so your judgment about what not to build matters as much as what the team ships.

About DataSnipper

DataSnipper is the driving force behind an intelligent automation platform that’s transforming the world of audit and finance.

Founded in 2017, DataSnipper has skyrocketed and is now OFFICIALLY the fastest-growing software company in the Netherlands according to Deloitte Fast50 and recently achieved Unicorn status in our latest funding round. With over 400.000 users in 125+ countries and a second base in the heart of New York City, DataSnipper is shaking things up. And we’re not stopping there. At DataSnipper, we’re always on the lookout for innovators who think outside of the box. New ideas aren’t just welcomed at DataSnipper–they’re essential.

What your team owns

The Data Platform team works across three areas:

  • Data Platform: reliable, scalable infrastructure that gets the right data to the right place

  • Internal Analytics: a self-service platform so every team can be data-informed without a ticket

  • Customer-facing Analytics: the dashboards and exports customers use to see the value they get from DataSnipper

Concretely, you would be walking into billions of usage events flowing from our Excel Add-in, web apps and product backends through Azure Event Hubs into Snowflake; a dbt estate built on medallion principles and managed in dbt Cloud; Terraform-managed Snowflake and Azure infrastructure; and a set of product teams shipping AI agents faster than we can instrument them.

You will also find real, named open problems rather than a tidy platform: event capture mid-consolidation, multiple methods of user attribution, and a data quality layer that is designed but not yet built. We would rather tell you that up front.

What you will do

Lead the team

  • Lead a team of two data engineers through outcomes, not tasks: set clear goals with the team and trust them to figure out how

  • Make the team measurably better: raise the engineering bar, grow each engineer into bigger problems, and address performance issues directly when they arise

  • Run regular 1:1s, give clear and timely feedback, and own each engineer's goals and development

  • Foster a culture of experimentation, learning, documentation and operational excellence

  • Take part in hiring and help shape the team's scope as it evolves

Own direction and delivery

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Customer Success and GTM to shape the team's roadmap, turning vague data requests into scoped, well-defined work

  • Make the trade-offs a small team serving the whole company needs: what to build, what to defer, and when a request shouldn't become a pipeline

  • Set the technical direction and make the architectural calls that shape the team's systems

  • Keep Snowflake performance and cost, tech debt, dependencies and compliance obligations (audit logging, vulnerability remediation, Vanta evidence) visible and under control

  • Be the person other engineering teams come to when they need to instrument something new

Stay hands-on in the data platform

  • Contribute to the event ingestion architecture end to end: Azure Event Hubs, Snowpipe, Fivetran, and our shared Python/TypeScript event client libraries

  • Build and review dbt transformation pipelines that stay reliable as volume, source count and model complexity grow

  • Define and enforce event contracts and schemas so product teams can instrument new features without silent breakage downstream

  • Evolve the core data models (event, user, license, company) and integrate new sources such as product backends, MongoDB, HubSpot and billing

  • Guide reverse ETL and activation work that pushes modeled data back into HubSpot, MongoDB, Postgres and GTM reporting

What you bring

Leadership

  • At least 1 year leading engineers as a team lead or engineering manager: 1:1s, feedback, goal setting, performance, and development

  • An empowerment style of leadership: you lead through outcomes and trust, not by assigning tasks

  • Early evidence of growing engineers and raising a team's bar, and the willingness to address performance issues directly

  • Strong product aptitude: you can challenge the framing of a request, translate stakeholder needs into technical solutions, and make roadmap trade-offs


Data engineering

  • 7+ years in data engineering or a closely related backend/platform role, with a track record of owning a data platform area end to end

  • Deep SQL and strong Python, including query optimization and performance tuning on a cloud warehouse

  • Production experience with a cloud data warehouse (we use Snowflake) and a modern transformation framework (we use dbt)

  • Experience with event-driven / streaming ingestion and its failure modes: schema drift, duplication, late data, backfills

  • Experience on a cloud platform at the infrastructure level (we're on Azure; AWS/GCP transfers fine)

  • Solid data modeling fundamentals and the ability to defend a modeling decision to both engineers and business stakeholders

  • Experience operating data systems in production with a focus on reliability, observability and maintainability


How you work

  • Excellent communication in English and genuine comfort working directly with non-technical stakeholders

  • Bias to action, a strong sense of ownership, and the judgment to prioritize when demand exceeds capacity

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in a startup or scale-up, ideally as an early member of a data team

  • Experience hiring engineers or helping a team expand its scope

  • Experience with product analytics tooling (Mixpanel, RudderStack) and warehouse-native BI (Netspring/Optimizely Analytics, Omni, Embeddable, or similar)

  • Experience building data products for AI or agent consumption: semantic layers, metrics layers, MCP servers, or governed self-service access

  • Experience with Terraform, Docker and data governance at scale

  • Reverse ETL experience and familiarity with CRM data models (HubSpot, Salesforce) or customer success platforms


What we offer

  • Being part of one of the fastest-growing scale-ups in the Netherlands

  • Make an impact by disrupting the audit industry with us

  • A step into engineering management, with Engineering Manager scope on a small team

  • 28 vacation days

  • Excellent salary

  • Pension plan

  • Stock participation plan

  • Hybrid work (Amsterdam-based)

  • International team and environment

  • Daily lunch

  • Mental health support (OpenUp)

  • Social events and team activities

Recruitment steps

  1. Recruiter screen

  2. Hiring Manager interview

  3. System design interview

  4. Product interview

  5. Final interviews with Engineering leadership

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

As a member of our Security Operations Team, you will collaborate with a global team of engineers to monitor and respond to security events, lead security incidents as Incident Commander, and lead digital forensic investigations in support of Employee Relations, Legal, Compliance, or Information Security cases.

Although you will be focused on security incident response, you will also have the opportunity to create and maintain runbooks, and automated workflows, and assist in process refinement and implementation. You will collaborate with a diverse team of engineers, and key stakeholders on security initiatives across the company. Above all, your focus is bringing Security expertise to the table in a collaborative, humble, and practical manner.

Location: This role is open to candidates residing in Netherlands

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
  • You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
  • You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.

  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.

In this role, you will: 

  • Monitor security events and provide technical analysis on alerts
  • Lead information security incidents and employee insider investigations by developing the incident response strategy, lead the execution through incident closure, while providing incident updates to key stakeholders throughout the incident
  • Deliver security guidance clearly and concisely for incident response and insider threat initiatives
  • Coordinate the building of services, capabilities, integrations, and implementations of technologies to support security operations, incident response, and insider threat
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
  • Participate in our on-call rota covering weekends

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 5+ years of experience in Security Incident Response
  • Ability to communicate investigative findings and strategies to technical staff, executive leadership, and legal
  • Ability to build scripts or tools to support Samsara's investigation processes, with proficiency in Python
  • Mentor and train security operation engineers on data collection, analysis, and reporting technical analysis
  • Practical experience acting as a lead during security incident response, including monitoring and triaging alerts, and coordinating across teams
  • Understanding of analysis and forensics techniques on macOS, Windows, and Linux
  • Experience utilizing SIEM tools to perform log reviews
  • Experience in cloud architecture and security (AWS, GCP) and cloud-based services
  • Participation in an on-call rotation, with the potential to work outside standard business hours, including late evenings, when responding to high-severity incidents as part of our global incident response team.
  • This role will be part of our EMEA so your hours will be aligned to the UK. As an operational time you may be expected to work flexible hours around this to support the load of the team

An ideal candidate also has:

  • 2+ years of experience working on insider threat initiatives or employee investigations
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field - or relevant industry experience
  • GIAC Certified Incident Handler (GCIH) or similar Certification
  • Familiarity with common security frameworks and standards, including NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 27001, FedRAMP

raw.description:
The world of payment processing is rapidly evolving, and businesses are looking for loyal and strategic partners, to help them grow.

Meet Nuvei, the Canadian fintech company accelerating the business of clients around the world. Nuvei's modular, flexible and scalable technology allows leading companies to accept next-gen payments, offer all payout options and benefit from card issuing, banking, risk and fraud management services. Connecting businesses to their customers in more than 200 markets, with local acquiring in 50 markets, 150 currencies and 700 alternative payment methods, Nuvei provides the technology and insights for customers and partners to succeed locally and globally with one integration.

At Nuvei, we live our core values, and we thrive on solving complex problems. We’re dedicated to continually improving our product and providing relentless customer service.   We are always looking for exceptional talent to join us on the journey!

 

Your Mission 

We are looking for a Senior Director of Analytics & Business Intelligence to join our fast-growing Revenue Operations team. Reporting to our SVP of Global Revenue Operations, you will lead Nuvei’s Commercial reporting and x-functional performance analytics globally, across every segment, channel and vertical. This is a key leadership role responsible for a Commercial analytics suite spanning marketing analytics, revenue acquisition, portfolio and payment performance.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead Nuvei’s Commercial reporting and x-functional performance analytics globally, across every segment, channel and vertical
  • Own a Commercial analytics suite spanning marketing analytics, revenue acquisition, portfolio and payment performance
  • Deliver insights from data and complex signals in support of clear, actionable direction for stakeholders
  • Lead root cause analysis of segment, channel, vertical, client and Commercial performance to identify opportunities for revenue optimisation
  • Partner with stakeholders and domain SMEs for detailed diagnostics as needed
  • Standardise and operationalise dashboarding and KPIs across business units and for executive communications
  • Define business requirements and translate into a data, analytics and automation roadmap – migrate from static dashboarding to intelligent decision support
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement to increase speed, clarity and impact of reporting/analytical products

 

Qualifications

  • Player-coach with 15+ years’ experience in delivery of revenue forecasting and profitability analysis, within the payments industry - must
  • Track record of leading and mentoring a team of data analysts and BI developers
  • Experience delivering scalable reporting frameworks, including defining data models, KPIs, metrics and reporting standards
  • Experience with leading strategic, performance and operational analysis in support of business decision-making
  • Experience working with Salesforce, BI and leveraging AI tools/methodologies to improve productivity and dynamic decision-management

 

Benefits

Specific benefits and details about what compensation is included in the salary range listed above will vary depending on the applicant’s location and can be discussed in more detail during the interview process.

Nuvei is an equal-opportunity employer that celebrates collaboration and innovation and is committed to developing a diverse and inclusive workplace. The team at Nuvei is comprised of a wealth of talent, skill, and ambition. We believe that employees are happiest when they’re empowered to be their true, authentic selves. So, please come as you are. We can’t wait to meet you. 

Working Language 

  • English (written and spoken) is the language used most of the time, as work colleagues, clients, and strategic suppliers are geographically dispersed. 

****Our recruitment process may use automated tools, including AI, to support application management and candidate shortlisting.

The annual salary range for this role in the Netherlands is EUR 130,000 - EUR 170,000 (gross). This range represents the expected starting salary for candidates hired into this role in the specified location. If the position is filled in a different location, a different salary range may apply due to objective factors such as local labor market conditions and cost of living.

This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Nuvei and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and specific location. Applicants not located in the primary location may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

raw.title: Lead AI Engineer
raw.description:
We are AI builders

Since 2018, Enjins has done one thing: ship AI that works in production. From Utrecht and Berlin, we build machine learning systems, data infrastructure, and agentic AI layers for European tech companies, with a deliberate focus on climate and energy, where we believe the biggest technological shift of our generation should meet its most critical challenge.

We embed directly with the engineering teams of high-growth scale-ups like Crisp, PlanBlue, NextSense, and Groendus. We take ownership of the full technical lifecycle: from first architecture decision to a production-grade system running inside our partner's infrastructure, long after go-live.

The role

As Lead AI Engineer, you are the technical owner of client engagements. You architect the solution, ship it to production, and make sure it still performs a year later. Alongside the other Leads, you shape the engineering team and the way we build.

In practice:

  • Design AI roadmaps with client leadership and own them through to production
  • Create and implement the AI solution architectures to deliver on those roadmaps
  • Set and uphold Data Platform and MLOps standards across your client portfolio, so systems stay healthy after handover
  • Mentor engineers and weigh in on hiring, team growth, and accounts
  • Push our engineering practice forward, including how we use agentic coding workflows to build faster without compromising reliability. We test, document, and share what works, so the whole team levels up
  • Elevate our product mindset to ensure we build the right things, not just more things

Why a Lead role here, not somewhere else

You'll work across more stacks, clouds, and frontier frameworks in a year than most engineers see in five, with the collective knowledge of the whole team behind you, not the isolation of freelance work. And because our clients build grid software, energy forecasting, and climate infrastructure, you develop real domain expertise in energy and climate systems on top of production-grade AI engineering.

In your first months you'll join a client project alongside an experienced Enjins engineer, supported by a dedicated coach. Within half a year, you own the technical roadmap of at least one engagement, mentor engineers, and have a recognised voice in our Asset strategy.

Requirements

What matters most: you think in systems, own outcomes end-to-end, and grow the people around you.

  • 5+ years building and scaling data & AI solutions in production environments
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals: you write production-grade code and know your way around infrastructure (Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, data pipelines)
  • Mastery of at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, GCP) and experience leading MLOps/LLMOps architectures
  • Proven experience taking LLM-based or agentic systems to production
  • Experience mentoring engineers, overseeing delivery, and managing client accounts
  • You can translate technical complexity into clear decisions for non-technical stakeholders
  • Fluent in English and eligible to work in the Netherlands

Benefits

We publish our salary ranges and keep terms straightforward. No surprises.

Compensation

  • €5,950 - €7,800 gross per month (excl. holiday allowance, pension, bonus, equity, and AI-Leap benefits)
  • Annual performance bonus of 1.5 months' salary
  • Equity participation (VSOP)


Growth

  • AI-Leap: our structured development programme with a dedicated certification budget and a specialised track for Leads
  • 1-on-1 mentoring with our founders and external coaching to close your specific gaps


Team & culture

  • Office on the Oudegracht in Utrecht (note: not yet fully accessible for individuals with physical disabilities); hybrid setup
  • 28 vacation days, flexible across 3 national holidays
  • Monthly team events and the annual two-day Enjins Summer Summit on AI × Climate
  • OV-First travel policy, fully covered; meat-free catering
  • Apple MacBook Pro and the tools you need
